title: E-flat clarinet and number of keys on old clarinets
summary: He tried an E-flat clarinet and disliked it; they discuss key counts and rings on older Albert system clarinets.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: They used alto horn or baritone, brass? Yeah. I'm wondering too about the E-flat clarinet, if you ever played that or ever had one or tried to play it? No, I never played the E-flat.
I had gotten one and it needed a pan and I took it and kind of fixed it up and blow it on it and I didn't like it. It's so high. Yeah. And I just put it down.
I never worried about playing O-E-flat. Did the fingering bother you any?
Was it being closer together or did that bother you? Just the... Oh yeah, a little. Because you have to get used to that close to finger.

And I never intended to play that much for red, you know. So I never worried about the E-flat. Do you remember some of the older Albert Sardin's band? Albert Sardin's band, if they had less keys than they have now, do you remember like the first one you got? Or some of the older players, the ones that you saw, if they had... how many keys did yours have?
About 13 is it or something? No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. Well, some of them had 13 keys.
13 and 15. I believe that was the last 13. Did any of them have less than that even on them? Not that I know of.
That would be with no rings on it, Albert Sardin's band?
No ring at the top. No ring at the top. I had a ring on the lower joint. Yeah.
I believe, I think I had one of them. I don't know.
I don't know. I don't know.
I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I believe, I think I had one with no rings at all. I think Piku's got one ring. Yeah, I believe I had one with no rings at all.
